To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the text and the inverted file can be compressed by 50% with no loss of performance, that the compressed index and the compressed text can be kept in memory, and that the compressed index can be kept on disk, while the text can be updated in compressed form.
the text of a document can be compressed to 50 percent of its original size, and the time to search the compressed document can be less than the time needed to search the uncompressed version.
compression of text and index can be combined to achieve a significant space reduction without any time penalty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the compression of the complete text retrieval system.
the following issues: (i) How can we compress the text of a document?
compression of the text and the associated index of a text retrieval system, and the use of these compressed files to speed up the retrieval process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compression is an important feature of any text retrieval system, and it can be used to reduce the storage space, the index building time, and the search time.
compression is an effective way to reduce the size of a text database.
compression can be used in text retrieval systems to reduce the storage requirements, to reduce the index build and query time, and to allow the text to be kept compressed all of the time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to compress the complete text of the TREC-4 collection by a factor of about 4.7, and the index by a factor of 4.5.
we have developed a complete system to store and retrieve text data that is more efficient in space, time and update than any other known system.
we have shown how to compress the index and the text of the next-generation text retrieval system without sacrificing search speed or update speed, and with a significant savings in storage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compression is not an impediment, but rather an aid, in text retrieval.
compression techniques can be used to improve performance of text retrieval systems.
compression is a key feature for text retrieval systems, and that the compression of the index is as important as the compression of the text itself.
